subject: Production inference latency spike impacting BrightMart checkout
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightmart.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Production inference latency spike affecting checkout

Sergio —

We're seeing a sudden jump in inference latencies from the Redwood hosted endpoint used by our checkout flow (orderflow_inference). p95 has moved from ~120ms to ~850ms and p99 is spiking above 2.2s. We're also seeing a small but growing number of 503s during peak minute windows. This started around 16:40 PST and is blocking a portion of orders from completing.

We've attached a short span of request IDs and traces for the last 20 minutes. Can your team triage immediately? Our SREs are standing by; we can route traffic to a fallback if you recommend it but need your remediation ETA.

Requirements from our side: keep throughput within our SLA and avoid a full outage — if you need to throttle, tell us the new expected RPS. BrightMart can accept temporary lower QPS for a short window but needs latency under 400ms p95.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Reliability
BrightMart

Attachments: sample_trace_1632.txt, logs_20261120.tar.gz
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightmart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production inference latency spike affecting checkout

Alicia — thanks for the rapid heads-up and for the traces. We're on it. Quick summary of next steps from Redwood:

- Immediate triage: SRE + runtime team are looking at allocations and OOM/eviction patterns.
- Short-term mitigation (15-45m): if we confirm memory pressure / fragmentation, we'll shift BrightMart traffic to a lower-memory quantized model variant and enable a temporary routing rule to shed large batched requests. This will reduce p99 spikes but may lower throughput.
- Communication: I'll send status updates every 30 minutes until we have a durable fix.

Laura, Aditya — can you pull the allocator histograms and per-pod OOM traces, and start a rolling restart plan for serving nodes in us-west-2? Marissa, please coordinate credit/compensation options and update BrightMart's CS ticket with an ETA.

Alicia — we'll aim to get you an ETA within 20 minutes. If you can forward any additional request IDs (especially 503s) that will help correlate traces.

— Sergio
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production inference latency spike affecting checkout — initial SRE findings

Sergio / Aditya — initial findings after a quick probe:

- Symptom: correlated increase in p95/p99 and periodic 503s on a subset of pods serving the orderflow_inference model.
- Evidence: JVM-level logs (attached) show repeated device allocation retries and segmented allocations failing with "out of GPU memory" even though aggregated usage reported <95% on the host.
- Hypothesis: GPU device memory fragmentation on the inference allocator leading to transient OOMs and eviction cascades when large context requests arrive. Not a single big allocation — rather many small frees/allocs and slab fragmentation.

Immediate actions I'm enacting now (start time 17:30 PST):
1) Mark affected serving pool as "degraded" and shift 60% of incoming BrightMart traffic to a fallback pool with a smaller, quantized model variant.
2) Begin a controlled rolling restart of 6/18 serving replicas suspected of heap/allocator fragmentation. Restarts will be staggered by 45s to avoid a thundering herd.
3) Apply a temporary allocator patch that forces coalescing of recently freed blocks (non-persistent tweak) to reduce fragmentation risk; this is reversible.

Attachments: runbook_gpu_mem-frag.pdf — contains the exact checklist for rolling restarts and the rollback procedure. Logs attached: logs_20261120.tar.gz.

I'll post back with tracer spans after the first two restarts complete.

— Laura
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightmart.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production inference latency spike affecting checkout — mitigation plan

Alicia — quick technical note for BrightMart and confirmation of actions:

- We are routing ~60% of BrightMart checkout traffic to a smaller quantized variant (orderflow_inference-q8v2) to reduce per-request GPU working set. Expected impact: p99 reduction to under 600–700ms, p95 ~250–360ms, QPS capacity reduced by ~30%.
- We are disabling prefix cache for requests above 2k tokens for the affected pool to reduce dynamic allocation churn (this is the main tradeoff).
- We're also applying a non-invasive allocator tuning flag that encourages slab defragmentation during low-load windows.

Timeline: config changes applied at 17:40 PST; rolling restarts will complete ~18:05 PST if no regressions. We'll keep a small canary and monitor for re-introduced fragmentation.

Operational note: this is a runtime-level mitigation; engineering will follow with a code-level allocator durability fix and better observability (heap fragmentation histograms per pod) in the coming days.

Let me know if you need us to route to Dedicated capacity while we fix — that would be a higher-cost but quick isolation path.

— Aditya
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

Thanks — that plan sounds reasonable. Two asks:

1) ETA: can you confirm when p95 is expected to be below 400ms? You mentioned 250–360ms expected on the fallback variant — when will traffic be fully on that route?
2) Credits: BrightMart will expect some SLA remediation if we record sustained violations. Please flag the account team with an estimated exposure window.

Also attaching one more trace where a checkout request got a 503 and includes the full injector header.

Alicia

Subject: Exec note — BrightMart production latency escalation (summary & request)

Team — summary of the BrightMart incident and asks for exec approval:

Incident summary:
- Start: 2026-11-20T16:40 PST — BrightMart reported p95/p99 regression and intermittent 503s in checkout.
- Root cause hypothesis: GPU device memory fragmentation within the hosted serving pool led to transient OOMs and eviction cascades when large context requests arrived.
- Immediate mitigations applied: routed traffic to orderflow_inference-q8v2 (smaller quantized variant), disabled prefix cache for >2k token requests, and performed a rolling restart on 6/18 replicas. Observed p95 reduce to ~280ms and p99 to ~650ms within 20 minutes of mitigations.

Customer impact and exposure: BrightMart experienced ~22 minutes of p95/p99 violations during the peak window (several 503s). We've logged request ids and traces; BrightMart will require SLA remediation evaluation.

Asks for leadership:
1) Approve a customer credit of up to $20,000 (estimate) as a proactive gesture while we complete the root-cause postmortem. Marissa — please confirm exact credit amount based on BrightMart's contract terms.
2) Approve a postmortem and customer readout timeline: initial RCA to customer within 72 hours, full postmortem in 10 business days.
3) Sign-off to prioritize an allocator durability fix (engineering spike + Q/A) in next sprint and fund an observability project for per-pod fragmentation histograms.

I'll coordinate the external readout and have a draft RCA ready for your review by Monday. Thoughts?

— Sergio
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
